A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AgentTrek and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices A-K. The retained experiments and supplementary material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original agent-training results on WebArena, ScreenSpot, and Multimodal-Mind2Web, together with tutorial-guidance, evaluator-validation, and data-scaling experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical studies, including the appendix experiments, and reports a revised WebArena result.

M1.justification: The tutorial-filtering, standardization, guided-replay, trajectory-evaluation, and agent-training pipeline remains the same. V2's dedicated text-agent subsection describes the AXTree/Playwright approach already used in v1 Section 3.1 and Appendix F; it does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use RedPajama-derived web trajectories and evaluate on WebArena, web-only ScreenSpot, and the same Multimodal-Mind2Web splits. V2's 127 websites and 11 categories were already reported in v1 Section 4.2. The scaling experiment also already appears in v1 Appendix I.

E2.justification: The WebArena comparison drops CodeLlama-7B-Instruct and AutoWebGLM (In-domain RFT) from v1 Table 5 to v2 Table 4. Synatra-CodeLlama-7B and AutoWebGLM (OOD SFT) remain. The corresponding ScreenSpot and Mind2Web comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated text-agent configuration changes from Qwen2 at 7B, 32B, and 72B in v1 Section 3.1 to Qwen2.5 at 7B and 32B in v2 Section 2.3.3. This aligns the description with v1's existing result-table labels and does not establish that experiments were rerun. Training-trajectory counts, the classifier's 95:5 split, and benchmark evaluation protocols are retained.

E4.justification: V1 Table 2's diagnostic comparison of prefilter, LLM-labeler, and FastText precision, recall, and F1 is removed, although some filter-performance summaries remain in prose. The tutorial-guidance comparison, evaluator confusion matrix, failed-replay case, and scaling study are retained. V2 Figure 7 redisplays existing scaling results rather than establishing a new experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new scaling plot adds no uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct with AgentTrek WebArena score changes from 16.26 in v1 Table 5 to 22.40 in v2 Table 4 without an accompanying explanation. Removed baseline and filter-table entries reduce reported results. Section 4 changes the tutorial gain from over 230% to 23% despite retaining 63 versus 208 successful trajectories. ScreenSpot, Mind2Web, and appendix scaling values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: No new theorem, proof, assumption, or substantive mathematical definition appears. V2's indexed action and reasoning sequences restate the existing evaluator inputs, and Appendix C retains the same cost calculation.

C1.justification: V1's abstract emphasizes improved grounding and planning; v2 explicitly claims state-of-the-art performance on named textual and visual benchmarks. The automated tutorial-based synthesis and cost-efficiency contributions remain the same, with existing multimodal capabilities and costs made more prominent.

C2.justification: V2 newly interprets the existing scaling results as approaching human-annotated Mind2Web performance, citing 45.0% versus 47.7%. It also adds explanations of structured text-agent interactions and a Research Challenges paragraph identifying adaptation to changing websites and coverage beyond 11 categories as future needs.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies prefilter length bounds of 200-5000 words and tutorial-related URL-pattern examples. It omits v1's first-38k-word matching detail, positive/negative validation-count breakdown, and positional-encoding discussion. These change the documented implementation detail without establishing a changed filtering procedure. Appendix prompts, action mappings, cost details, and the project link remain available.

R1.justification: V2 adds BAGEL and NNetNav and positions AgentTrek within existing synthetic-trajectory-generation efforts. It also adds the Qwen2.5 technical report and removes references including Brown et al., Li et al. (2023), Playwright documentation, and RoFormer. This is a limited but substantive update to positioning and citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, results discussion, analysis, and related work undergo extensive rewriting. Section 2.3 is reorganized around visual agents, textual agents, and training; training details move from the experimental setup, and the analysis and related-work structures change. Most appendix prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds a scaling plot using existing results, removes the filter-performance table, relocates several figures and tables, and places a compact WebArena table beside its discussion. Captions and conference headers change. Existing schematic, example, distribution, and appendix graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves readability, clarifies the text/vision training paths, and acknowledges relevant synthetic-data work. However, it removes filter diagnostics and comparison entries, introduces the incorrect 23% tutorial-gain statement, and leaves the WebArena revision from 16.26 to 22.40 unexplained. The clearer exposition is a real benefit, but the accompanying losses and uncertainties in empirical reporting prevent a confident net quality judgment.
